title: 64-char local-part truncation silently eats {RUN_ID} digits for the two longest-slug confirmation scenarios, so fast same-vacancy re-runs collide as duplicate applications
evidence:

The server's `shared/email.is_valid` rejects `/` in local parts and caps them at 64 — substituting the raw slug makes every `{SCENARIO}` email fail validation before the scenario exercises anything."

edge-cases/stacked-conditionals-student-firsttime.yaml: "  email: \"stacked+{SCENARIO}-{RUN_ID}@example.com\"" (prefix 8 + slug 49 + '-' + 10-digit epoch = 68 chars) and "expected_outcome: confirmation"

          form_pages.view_duplicate_application_page(" — a duplicate renders the duplicate page, not [data-testid=confirmation-page].
detail: Right-truncating the whole local part at 64 keeps only 6 of 10 RUN_ID epoch digits for stacked-conditionals (68 chars) and 8 for coapplicant-same-email (66). A same-vacancy re-run within ~2.8h/100s reuses the email, hits application_vacancy_id_email_key, and the confirmation-expected scenario falsely fails on the duplicate page. recommended_fix: Amend SKILL.md:170 to truncate only the sanitised slug so the local part fits 64, always preserving the literal prefix and the full '-{RUN_ID}' suffix; state the truncation order explicitly.
